facts.text: The README names Ubuntu 64-bit 20.04 as the prerequisite.
The README names ROS Noetic as the prerequisite.
The README installs ros-noetic-hector-trajectory-server, ros-noetic-slam-gmapping and ros-noetic-navigation with apt-get.
The shipped launch includes gazebo_ros empty_world.launch with worlds/warehouse.world, paused=false and gui=true.
warehouse.world sets the physics type to ode.
The launch spawns the pioneer3dx model from urdf/pioneer3dx.xacro and starts robot_state_publisher under the /pioneer3dx namespace.
The shipped launch starts slam_gmapping, move_base, rviz and hector_trajectory_server; its key_control node block is commented out.
The shipped launch starts move_base at the root namespace with respawn true and no remap.
The key_control node block in the shipped launch is inside an XML comment, so the teleop is not started by default.
The Pioneer 3DX differential-drive plugin sets commandTopic cmd_vel, odometryTopic odom, robotNamespace /, wheelSeparation 0.32, wheelDiameter 0.18, wheelAcceleration 0 and updateRate 100.0.
key_control.cpp includes geometry_msgs/Twist.h.
TeleopTurtle's constructor advertises geometry_msgs::Twist on the relative topic "cmd_vel" with queue size 1.
The teleop reads the scale_linear and scale_angular parameters with constructor defaults 2.0; they are not device bounds, and the clone states no numeric cmd_vel range.

keyLoop sets linear_ and angular_ to the per-key literals 0.7, 0.3, 0.0, -0.3 or -0.0, publishes twist.linear.x as l_scale_*linear_ and twist.angular.z as a_scale_*angular_ only after a recognized key, and the q key returns without publishing a zero.
The package builds exactly one executable, key_control, from src/key_control.cpp.
The laser sensor is configured with 360 samples, 0.0 to 6.28319 rad, a 0.120 to 10.0 m range, a 5 Hz update rate and topicName scan.
The IMU sensor is configured at 10 Hz with its Gazebo ROS plugin at 20 Hz on topicName imu.
The local costmap observation source is named scan, declares data_type LaserScan and uses the relative topic scan.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.
GazeboRosDiffDrive subscribes to its command topic with cmdVelCallback on the plugin's own callback queue.
GazeboRosDiffDrive connects UpdateChild to the world-update begin event.

When seconds_since_last_update is greater than update_period_, UpdateChild calls getWheelVelocities and, when wheel_accel is 0 or a wheel is within 0.01 of its target speed, sets both wheel joint velocities.
getWheelVelocities derives both wheel speeds from the stored x_ and rot_.
cmdVelCallback stores linear.x in x_ and angular.z in rot_.
QueueThread serves the plugin's callback queue with a 0.01 s wall-clock wait while the plugin is alive.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned responses with no physics step, wheel integration, sensor model or wall-clock pacing

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers the declared /cmd_vel publication and the two companion Gazebo services, and runs no Gazebo physics, differential-drive plugin, laser, IMU or gmapping/move_base node

the fake records the published Twist but has no robot pose, wheel state, sensor sample or physics timestep; it cannot establish motion, arrival or stopping; the cmd_vel receipt reports the values it sent, not a measurement

the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets and /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports; it runs no Gazebo World::Step, and its GetPhysicsProperties numbers are placeholders

no unpause is bound. Stopping publishers does not clear the plugin's stored x_ and rot_ (gazebo_ros_diff_drive.cpp:335-340); UpdateChild applies them again when updates resume (:269-289, speeds from :324-333). Publishing zero can replace those fields but is unacknowledged and is not proof they are clear. move_base starts at the root namespace with respawn true (warehouse_simulation.launch:45-60) and this package cannot cancel it. Before any manual unpause the operator prevents that respawn and clears or reinitializes the retained command outside MHS

move_base's velocity output topic is set outside the clone (the navigation stack); started at the root namespace without a remap it is expected on /cmd_vel, a second commander of the same plugin (not cited)

while pause is true, ordinary World::Step updates are suspended (World.cc:835-854), so /odom, /scan, /imu and /clock are not produced by those updates; a pending step (stepInc > 0), a manual WorldControl step or a Gazebo reset (needsReset) still calls Update. The read-back observes only IsPaused(). The package declares no read of those topics and the device resource reads no topic
another client can unpause or step the world after the e-stop: the Gazebo GUI the shipped launch opens (gui true), a WorldControl message, or any ROS client. MHS does not read the paused flag again
the read-back needs the ODE engine (warehouse.world sets ode): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held
the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.9.3 (Noetic) and 11 releases the companion citations name; rosbridge cannot read their versions
upstream timing values (the drive plugin's updateRate 100.0, the 5 Hz laser and the 10 Hz IMU with its 20 Hz plugin) are source facts, not this fake's timing
only /cmd_vel and the two companion world services are exposed; /scan, /odom, /imu, /tf, /map, the move_base action and the Gazebo reset and spawn services are NOT COVERED

operator_required.name: publish_cmd_vel
operator_required.reason: the pinned teleop sets angular_ to the per-key literals 0.3, -0.3 or 0.0 and multiplies by scale_angular (default 2.0); the clone states no numeric cmd_vel angular.z range or clamp, so the operator supplies the signed deployment envelope

operator_required.name: publish_cmd_vel
operator_required.reason: the pinned teleop sets linear_ to the per-key literals 0.7, 0.0 or -0.0 and multiplies by scale_linear (default 2.0); the clone states no numeric cmd_vel linear.x range or clamp, so the operator supplies the signed deployment envelope

safe_state.description: get_physics_properties read pause true (IsPaused). Ordinary World::Step updates stay suspended while that flag is true, except stepInc > 0 or a Gazebo reset (needsReset). Not a measured standstill. Other clients can unpause; MHS does not read the flag again. No unpause is bound. Before any manual unpause the operator prevents publisher respawn, including move_base, and clears or reinitializes stored x_ and rot_. Publishing zero is unacknowledged and does not prove they are clear.
